title: Self-Managing DRAM: A Low-Cost Framework for Enabling Autonomous and Efficient DRAM Maintenance Operations
problem: DRAM maintenance operations (refresh, RowHammer protection, memory scrubbing) are controlled by the memory controller, requiring DRAM interface and system modifications to implement new techniques. This dependency on DRAM standards development slows adoption of new DRAM architectural innovations.
motivation: Enable rapid innovation in DRAM architecture by allowing autonomous in-DRAM maintenance operations without requiring system-wide modifications.
method: Self-Managing DRAM (SMD) transfers maintenance operation control from the memory controller to the DRAM chip through a single DRAM interface modification: SMD chips reject memory controller accesses to regions under maintenance while allowing accesses to other regions. This enables autonomous maintenance and overlaps maintenance latency in one region with data access latency in another region.
key_novelty: Transferring autonomous maintenance operation control to DRAM chip with minimal interface changes, enabling new maintenance mechanisms without modifying memory controller or system components.
contributions: Low-cost DRAM architecture enabling autonomous in-DRAM maintenance with no new DDRx pins
Achieves 4.1% average speedup across 20 four-core memory-intensive workloads
Minimal overhead: 0.4% row activation latency and 1.1% of DRAM chip area
Guarantees forward progress for rejected accesses while enabling maintenance parallelization
